- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Model underestimates prices in late forecast periods, particularly when true values show upward momentum; adjust final 5–10 days upward by 3–7%.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes; apply a dampening factor (e.g., reduce peak values by 5–10% if preceded by >10% rise).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts decline after upticks; add a slight upward bias (1–3%) to forecasts following strong upward moves.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high in early days and too low in late days; apply a “sloped correction” — linearly reduce forecast from start to end by 1–3% per day.
- Model fails to capture seasonal or event-driven volatility; add a volatility buffer (±2–5%) to forecasts during high-activity periods (e.g., policy announcements, auction dates).
